methodological_rigor.justification: Two syngeneic immune-competent schwannoma models (CPA and sciatic nerve), both sexes 1:1, with Gluc reporter-based tumor tracking, caliper measurement, and auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing. Mechanistic dissection includes FITC-antibody delivery imaging, MVD/pericyte-coverage and perfusion quantification, flow cytometry of TILs, multiplex cytokine ELISA, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, CD8 and NK depletion, NKG2D blockade, and scRNA-seq on 4 human VS (3 naive, 1 bevacizumab-treated). Appropriate statistics (repeated measures two-way ANOVA, Kaplan-Meier log-rank, linear mixed-effects for ABR, Student t/Mann-Whitney for comparisons) with stated n per group and independent replication (>=3 experiments). Limitations include n=1 bevacizumab-treated human sample for scRNA-seq.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study with scRNA-seq validation in human VS tissues; Oxford LoE 5. However, clinical translational relevance is high: NF2-SWN has an unmet need, bevacizumab response is partial (30-40%) and not durable, and the study identifies a rational anti-PD1 + anti-VEGF combination with hearing preservation in immunocompetent models and mechanistic NKG2D dependence. Directly informs design of translational trials including salvage ICI for bevacizumab-refractory patients.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal study aligned with ARRIVE reporting expectations; explicit ethics approval (MGH IACUC Protocol #2016N00004), Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary referenced, randomized group assignment described, sex balance documented, antibody catalog and clone details provided (Supplementary Table 1), Source Data files referenced for each figure. scRNA-seq processing details (Cell Ranger 5.0.1, Seurat v4, UMAP) are specified. Explicit ARRIVE compliance statement is not shown in the normalized text, and deposition of scRNA-seq data is not visible in the excerpt.

novelty_literature.justification: First comprehensive preclinical investigation of ICI therapy in non-malignant vestibular schwannoma with hearing-preservation readouts, and first identification of NKG2D upregulation as the mechanistic driver of anti-VEGF-enhanced anti-PD1 efficacy in this context. Prior work is limited to subcutaneous schwannoma ICI experiments (modest effect) and a VS patient case report of anti-PD1 salvage; this study extends both with anatomically correct models, mechanistic dissection, and human scRNA-seq correlation.

writing_presentation.justification: Well organized around two clear questions posed in the Introduction, with logically ordered results (vascular normalization, combination efficacy, mechanism, human validation, salvage use). Figures are multi-panel but clearly legended and link to source data. Some methodological descriptions are dense and a grammatical fragment appears ('all animals showed.') in the ABR methods.

key_strengths: Two immune-competent syngeneic models (CPA and sciatic nerve) with both sexes and functional ABR-based hearing readouts
Mechanistic chain established via cytotoxicity assays, CD8/NK depletion, and NKG2D blockade showing NKG2D dependence
Anti-PD1 + anti-VEGF combination outperforms monotherapies in tumor growth, survival, and hearing preservation
Salvage experiment showing anti-PD1 controls tumors progressing on anti-VEGF
scRNA-seq on human NF2-SWN VS (including bevacizumab-treated) corroborates elevated cytotoxic profile of CD8+/NK cells
key_concerns: Human scRNA-seq bevacizumab arm is n=1, limiting human-data inference
No explicit ARRIVE checklist reference and sequence/repository accession not visible in normalized text
ICI ototoxicity assessed only up to 21 days; long-term safety in NF2-SWN patients will require clinical investigation
Mouse models, though anatomically relevant, may not fully recapitulate human NF2-SWN immune microenvironment
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous, mechanistically complete preclinical study addressing an unmet need in NF2-SWN with anatomically appropriate models, hearing preservation outcomes, and orthogonal mechanistic validation including human scRNA-seq; tier 1 with minor revisions is justified.
